scientific_evidence_class: UNPREREGISTERED_POSTHOC (already viewed both original development seeds, reset events and old Brier values; not prospective, not first-use)
question: Does suppressing just the already-observed native context reset in an archived continued native model preserve its old-world predictions at the expense of prequential predictions on subsequent observed consequences?
hypothesis: The same-event reset suppression should improve old-world historical readout but may impair new-world adaptation; this must be measured on precisely the same already-consumed subsequent witnesses, with full native source-based replay, before proposing a new memory mechanism.
controls: Unmodified NativeEpisodeExperience source-exact replay of each original prefix plus 16 original already-consumed JEPA2-05 episodes
A second exact no-intervention clone replay for deterministic negative control
Single reset-suppressed clone: _append and _update_context on the reset event in the prior context mixture instead of _load_context, with normal unmodified .observe continuation afterward

inputs.name: JEPA2-05 archival source, original code and checkpoints
inputs.provenance: This prior candidate was independently qualified Linux/Windows run 44629351965 (3/3) and includes prereg/diagnose source and exact G29 atlas

inputs.name: original parent frozen source
inputs.provenance: JEPA2-05 actual consumed development archives; no fresh source calls

changed_paths: .ice/code-atlas.* (G29 source-only generated seal, in separate final commit)

frozen_design.source: Already archived native original/continued checkpoint bytes; exact historical 16-event suffix in each; no generator/model API/network/simulator
frozen_design.data_budget: 16 consumed additional native witnesses per seed; 32 consumed prior old-world probes per seed; no new actions
frozen_design.order: Original unique episode ordered prefix + the exact 16 consumed suffix. Evaluate each postreset suffix event prequentially before model .observe using only preceding witnessed history; phase tags *not* exposed to predictor.
frozen_design.split: Original JEPA2-05 A positions 0..5, B 6..10, A-return 11..15, for evaluation labels only; reset at pre-observed ordinal 11/5.
frozen_design.compute_budget: <= 20 min per OS source-exact read-only replay, plus mandatory original inherited full regression <= 40 min per OS
frozen_design.evaluator: Mean of transition Brier + conditional terminal Brier over 2 for each postreset prequential witness; fixed 32 historical probes old-world native Brier using the existing native_old() definition.
frozen_design.capacity: One existing native model, plus source-equivalent disposable diagnostic clones; no extra experts, weights, sources, trainable policy, controller or checkpoint owner

metrics: Exact reproduction of source's original and final native state and published old historical Brier under tolerance 1e-10
Negative sham checkpoint byte-equivalence at every same-event replay step
Baseline and reset-suppressed postreset suffix prequential Brier, split phase A/B/A-return where observations exist
Actual and reset-suppressed final Brier on exactly the identical original 32 old probes
Count and ordinals of subsequent resets in reset-suppressed branch
CPU wall-process seconds and cross-OS metric agreement <=1e-10

classification_rules.supported: Retrospective source-exact mechanism/tradeoff audit only if independent checkpoint and published native Brier reproducibility, exact known reset ordinal, sham parity, original observed episode identities, no data leakage and phase/accounting controls all pass. Report full metrics irrespective of sign, never interpret as prospective science.
classification_rules.mixed: Retrospective mixed if one original seed shows better retention but worse adaptation or divergent phase sensitivity; neither no-reset nor actual claimed superior
classification_rules.negative: Retrospective negative if reset suppression fails to preserve old readout or worsens subsequent prequential Brier on both seeds, still retain full results
classification_rules.invalid: Reproduction fail on missing source file, source hash or identity mismatch, original/final Brier mismatch >1e-10, sham drift, unaccounted reset, nonfinite metric, unobserved source, extra action, or tree/atlas inconsistency
